entry.name: HRDexDB
entry.title: HRDexDB: A 4D Dexterous Grasping Dataset Across Human and Multiple Robot Embodiments
entry.summary: Paired human and teleoperated robot grasps (Allegro V5 Plus, Inspire RH56F1 and RH56DFTP, Robotiq 2F-85 on an xArm6) over 100 objects, filmed by a 23-camera rig with MANO hands and object 6D poses; built-in tactile only on the Allegro and Inspire F1 hands.
entry.hand: Human hand (no tactile); Allegro Hand V5 Plus (16 DoF), Inspire RH56F1, Inspire RH56DFTP, Robotiq 2F-85, each on an xArm6

sensor.note: Robot hands only. Allegro V5 Plus: raw/hand/tactile.npy (T, 4) int32, one value per fingertip sensor, ~99 Hz, 0 to ~1,800 counts. Inspire RH56F1 (right hand): raw/hand/right_tactile.npy, one dict per sample with normal_force, tangential_force and tangential_direction for 8 regions (little, ring, middle, index, thumb, palm_right, palm_middle, palm_left) = 24 scalars at 50 Hz. Inspire RH56DFTP: tactile.npy is empty in all 618 episodes; a per-actuator force.npy (T, 6) at ~50 Hz is present. Robotiq 2F-85: none. Units are not stated. Paper: readings too noisy or sparse to serve as contact labels.
sensor.model: Allegro Hand V5 Plus fingertip tactile sensors; Inspire RH56F1 built-in tactile; Inspire RH56DFTP finger force sensors

scale.text: Release: 2,703 sequences (441 human, 453 Allegro, 592 Inspire F1, 618 Inspire DFTP, 599 Robotiq) over 100 objects, ~14.9 h of synchronized 30 fps capture, 23 views; paper: 3,215 trials (541 human), 43.5M frames (all views)

entry.access: Hugging Face HRDexDB/HRDexDB, ungated, ~1.56 TB of per-sequence folders (per-camera mp4, raw .npy robot streams, MANO, object pose npz); single files can be fetched; Google Drive ZIP mirror also offered.
caveats: Grasping only: one grasp-and-lift task per sequence; robot trials teleoperated to reproduce a reference human grasp (no frame-level alignment between paired human and robot sequences).
No human tactile; the human hand is a MANO fit from multi-view video.
Inspire RH56DFTP tactile.npy is empty (0 elements) in all 618 released episodes; only a 6-channel force.npy with undocumented units is present, stored as unsigned 16-bit wrap-around (65,535 = -1).
Tactile units, sensor-to-channel mapping and calibration are not documented for any hand; the paper calls the Allegro and Inspire readings too noisy or sparse for contact labels.
Many raw .npy files (arm streams, Inspire F1 hand and tactile, Robotiq hand, teleop) are pickled object arrays and need allow_pickle to load.
Release (2,703 sequences) is smaller than the paper's 3,215 trials; all 453 released Allegro sequences are labelled successful, while the paper reports 52 Allegro failures.
The metadata catalog (metadata/episodes.parquet, 2,104 rows) does not cover the Robotiq sequences; 33 Robotiq folders lack raw/ and 36 lack calibration files.
Videos are 2048x1536 MPEG-4 Part 2 (not H.264), ~230-840 MB per sequence (median, by embodiment) across 22-23 views.

tracking.system: HaMeR 2D keypoints in calibrated views -> triangulation -> MANO fit (shape calibrated by SAM3 silhouettes)
tracking.note: human sequences; per-frame MANO mesh (.obj) and params (.json, incl. 21 joints)

tracking.system: SAM3 masks + FoundPose init + GoTrack multi-view 6D tracking
tracking.note: all embodiments; object_6d_pose_v1/v2 npz, one 4x4 per video frame

tracking.system: robot hand joint states and commands

tracking.note: every robot hand is mounted on an xArm6
teleoperation of robot fingers; raw glove skeletons released only for Inspire DFTP and Robotiq sequences

other: camera intrinsics/extrinsics (+ per-frame ego extrinsics for the helmet)

sources: https://huggingface.co/datasets/HRDexDB/HRDexDB raw files of human/apple/0, allegro_v5/apple/3, inspire_f1/apple/0, inspire_dftp/apple/0, robotiq_2f85/apple/0 and tactile/force files of 9 more robot sequences
unconfirmed: episodes=2,703 counted from sequence folders in the HF tree (human 441, allegro_v5 453, inspire_f1 592, inspire_dftp 618, robotiq_2f85 599); metadata/episodes.parquet lists 2,104 (no Robotiq); paper: 3,215 trials (541 human, 539 Allegro, 743 Inspire F1, 791 Inspire DFTP, 601 Robotiq); GitHub README: 2.1K; HF card: 3.2K.

hours=14.9 derived: catalog num_frames for 2,104 sequences sum to 1,275,339 and Robotiq raw/timestamps/frame_id.npy lengths (568 of 599 sequences) sum to 334,860; 1,610,199 frames / 30 fps = 14.9 h. Excludes ~31 Robotiq sequences without timestamps.
frames=43.5M is the paper's figure and counts images over all camera views.
subjects=1: paper says 'a human subject' / 'A human participant'; not stated as a count. Number of teleoperators not stated.
tasks=1: single grasp-and-lift task type; not a stated count. Paper: 23 of 33 GRASP-taxonomy grasp types.
scene_types=['lab']: one capture platform (21-camera rig around a workspace); no scene count is stated.

Cameras: paper says 21-camera exocentric rig + stereo helmet (human) or static stereo egocentric cameras (robot). In the files the helmet pair is 25452062/25452066 (ego_calib.json has per-frame extrinsics); human and Inspire F1 sequences carry 23 streams, Allegro and Inspire DFTP 22 (no 22684210), Robotiq 22-23 (adds 26256735/26256742, lacks 23029839). Camera models not stated. All streams 2048x1536 mpeg4 tagged 30 fps (metadata/cameras.parquet, one human mp4 probed).
raw/timestamps/timestamp.npy steps median 0.030 s (~33 Hz) in the sampled Allegro, Inspire F1 and DFTP sequences while the mp4 files are tagged 30 fps; Robotiq steps are 0.0333 s.

Tactile and force rates are medians of the time stamps in the sampled files (Allegro hand ~99 Hz, Inspire F1 tactile 50.0 Hz, Inspire DFTP hand ~49.7 Hz). Inspire F1 tangential_direction ranges 0-359 with -1 when unloaded, i.e. likely degrees (not stated). F1 thumb_normal_force reached exactly 3000 in cactus/3 (possible clip).
Inspire DFTP force.npy: values above 32,767 occur and read as small negatives when reinterpreted as int16 (e.g. 65,525 = -11); the channel order (6 actuators) is not documented.
Object pose translations are ~0.3-0.6 in magnitude (consistent with meters; unit not stated). C2R.npy is a 4x4 the official code inverts to get robot_from_world.

Human success labels are null in the catalog (paper: all human trials succeed). Release success counts: Allegro 453/453, Inspire F1 423 true / 164 false / 5 null, Inspire DFTP 387 / 231, Robotiq grasp_result.json 474 / 81 (555 files).

episodes.subject: robot: Allegro V5 Plus on xArm6, teleoperated (MANUS + Vive)
episodes.why: Contact on all 4 fingertip channels, each more than 100 counts above rest (rest 0) for over 1 s: ch0 2.3 s (peak 421), ch1 2.5 s (604), ch2 2.7 s (589), ch3 3.8 s (1,133). Contact is at 2.1-9.0 s on the video clock. Of 40 scanned Allegro sequences (one per object, successful, 10-60 s), only this one and orange/0 have all 4 channels in contact for at least 1 s. Grasp succeeded. Video timestamps have 442 rows with frame_id 1-442 and no gaps, matching the 442 video frames. Tactile is 1,461 rows (~97 Hz), monotonic, no NaN, and starts 2.5 s before the first video frame.

episodes.subject: robot: Inspire RH56F1 (right) on xArm6, teleoperated (MANUS + Vive)
episodes.why: Strongest multi-finger F1 contact among 44 checked F1 sequences. Normal force exceeds rest + 100 for 4.3 s on middle (peak 513), 4.6 s on index (1,391) and 4.6 s on thumb (574), at 10.5-16.1 s on the video clock. Tangential force and direction move on the same regions (direction 0-359). Ring stays below 30 and little stays at 0 / -1. The three palm regions read 0 / -1 for the whole clip; this matches the release, where palm normal force never exceeded 17 in the 44 checked F1 sequences. All 24 values are present in every sample: 1,110 rows at 50 Hz, monotonic, no NaN. Grasp succeeded. cactus/3 has more regions touched (ring, middle, index, thumb), but only ring and thumb stay in contact for at least 1 s.

episodes.subject: robot: Inspire RH56DFTP on xArm6, teleoperated (MANUS gloves + Vive tracker)
episodes.why: All 6 force channels rise above rest + 100 for 5.4-6.8 s at 10.1-16.8 s on the video clock (peaks 1,030 / 2,722 / 2,372 / 1,352 / 1,436 / 398, after undoing the uint16 wrap of negatives). Ch4 also rises at 5.1 s, before contact. Of the 4 DFTP sequences checked, this is the only one with all 6 channels active. Grasp succeeded. force.npy has 1,159 rows (~49.5 Hz), monotonic, no NaN. tactile.npy is (0,) here, as in all 618 DFTP sequences, so it cannot be shown.

sample.fetch_estimate: ~190 MB. Needed per episode: raw/ + cam_param/ + C2R.npy + grasp_result.json (allegro_v5/yellow_wash_tub/0 1.1 MB, inspire_f1/brown_ramen/10 2.0 MB, inspire_dftp/apple/0 10.4 MB, from the HF tree API), object_6d_pose_v2 npz (~0.1 MB each) and two camera MP4s per episode (median sizes 19 / 28 / 35 MB, so ~165 MB in total; cameras.parquet byte_size). All 22-23 views would cost 413 + 617 + 751 MB = ~1.8 GB. Already local: inspire_dftp/apple/0 raw (raw_sample/), plus the 43 MB tactile scan of 80 sequences (scan/). Re-hosted media: the 2048x1536 MPEG-4 Part 2 views must be re-encoded to H.264 at a lower resolution, estimated at a few MB per view per clip. Episode JSON: full-rate touch is 1,461x4 + 1,110x24 + 1,159x6 values, far below 2 MB.
sample.rules_applied: Tasks: the release has 1 task (grasp and lift), at most 6, so it is taken. Episodes: with 3 tasks or fewer the rule is 2-3 per task and at least 3 in total, so 3 episodes. They come from different embodiments and different objects (wash tub, ramen pack, apple), which stand in for the different subjects and scenes the release does not have. Only embodiments with a touch channel were eligible: Allegro V5 Plus (tactile), Inspire RH56F1 (tactile) and Inspire RH56DFTP (force). Human sequences (MANO fit from video) and Robotiq 2F-85 (gripper position only) have no tactile or force channel, so they cannot show contact. Candidates: successful sequences of 10-60 s from metadata/episodes.parquet, one per object, 40 random per hand (random_state=0). Contact means more than 100 counts above the median of the first 5% of samples, for 1 s or longer. Length: the three timestamp spans are 13.4 / 20.0 / 22.7 s, all within 10-60 s, so no window is cut. Budget: within 2 MB JSON, ~30 MB media per episode and 20 GB download.
deviations: No human or Robotiq 2F-85 episode: they have no touch channel. Each robot episode names its paired human sequence (metadata/pairings.parquet) for a possible later side-by-side.

inspire_dftp/apple/0: tactile.npy is empty, as in the whole DFTP release, so only force.npy is shown. inspire_f1/brown_ramen/10: little finger and the three palm regions are flat (0, direction -1) for the whole clip, as palm regions are across the scanned release.

checks.method: Pickled .npy files (F1 right_tactile) read with a restricted unpickler that allows only numpy _reconstruct/ndarray/dtype/scalar. Other arrays read with allow_pickle=False. Episode list from metadata/episodes.parquet (success == True, 300-1800 frames).
checks.scan: Fetched raw/hand tactile + time for 40 Allegro and 40 F1 sequences (43 MB, ~/data/ext/hrdexdb/scan/), plus the 4 Allegro, 4 F1 and 4 DFTP sequences already in raw_sample/. Allegro: 2 of 40 scanned have all 4 channels in contact for at least 1 s; 7 have 3. F1 (40 scanned + 4 in raw_sample/): 35 of 44 have at most one region in contact for at least 1 s; 28 have none. Two have 3 regions: brown_ramen/10, and yellow_wash_tub/0 with peaks below 180. This matches the paper's statement that the tactile readings are noisy or sparse.
checks.video_timeline: Official code (hrdexdb_io.py load_video_timeline / common.py load_video_frame) maps raw/timestamps row i to video frame frame_id[i]-1. Allegro yellow_wash_tub/0: 442 rows = 442 video frames. F1 brown_ramen/10: 669 rows with frame_id 1-669 (a few local reorderings such as 2,4,6,3,7), while the videos have 659 frames, so the last ~10 ids have no frame. All 9 F1 sequences checked show such an excess (10-24 rows). DFTP apple/0: 754 rows vs 755 frames. The timestamp step is 30 ms (~33 Hz), although the MP4s are tagged 30 fps.
checks.dftp_force_wrap: inspire_dftp/apple/0 force.npy raw min/max 0 / 65,535; values > 32,767 converted as x - 65,536 (min -26 after the conversion).

visualization.detail: 4 fingertip readings as 4 painted 4x4 pads on a schematic right hand (back view, thumb lower left); column order assumed index, middle, ring, thumb from the Allegro URDF joint order (not documented, not confirmable from the data). Latest sample at or before each video-frame time; raw counts, not tared; colour range = episode max rounded up. Plot: per-region values.

8 named regions (thumb, index, middle, ring, little fingertips; palm_left/middle/right as palm L/M/R) as painted pads; pad colour = normal_force; arrow = tangential_force at tangential_direction read as degrees CCW from the panel x axis (unit and zero direction not documented), ring = normal_force. Plots: normal force per region (region sums), tangential force per region, tangential direction per region (gaps where -1). Palm L/M/R left-right placement in name order (side not documented).

6 per-actuator readings, uint16 wrap-around undone (x - 65536 for x > 32767), as one pad per actuator on a schematic right hand (thumb bend at the thumb, thumb rotation at the thumb base); order little, ring, middle, index, thumb bend, thumb rotation assumed from the official loader's position/action order. Pads clipped at 0; plots: signed force per actuator, plus actuator positions.
